assumptions: The metric was interpreted as average authorization latency of failed payment attempts (the catalog only exposes p95 latency, so the average was computed with custom SQL).
The requested time window was 2024-10-31 to 2026-10-31, interpreted as 'the past two years'.
The period actually covered by the data is 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31.
caveats: Data starts on 2026-08-01; the requested two-year window was clipped, so results cover only about three months.

Part of this answer uses custom SQL written by the AI, outside the governed semantic layer. It was validated (read-only, governed views only, role filters applied) before running, but its logic has not been reviewed like the governed metrics.

Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once; the duplicates were removed in the clean view (first ingestion kept).

Missing issuer IDs: 8.0% of Meridian Bank's card attempts in 2026-08 (2,856 of 35,507) have no issuer_id, where 0% is expected. Issuer-level results for this scope are understated. These rows were kept and shown as '(missing)' issuer.

Volume spike 18 Oct to 31 Oct: attempt volume was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days. Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: Technical failures averaged 17,422 ms of authorization latency across 23,887 failed attempts.
Customer drop-offs averaged 12,018 ms across 45,910 failed attempts.
Risk declines averaged 3,204 ms across 12,544 failed attempts.
Issuer declines averaged 2,559 ms across 37,617 failed attempts.
The latency figures were computed by custom SQL over failed attempts only, from the cleaned attempts view.
The attempt data only begins on 2026-08-01, so the 'past two years' covers about three months (2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31).

response.headline: Failed payments do not share one average authorization time: it depends on why they failed, with technical failures averaging 17,422 ms and customer drop-offs 12,018 ms, versus 3,204 ms for risk declines and 2,559 ms for issuer declines.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Look at the latency distribution and timeout rates for technical and customer drop-off failures, and compare against configured timeout thresholds.
hypotheses.rationale: Both categories average several times the latency of issuer and risk declines, which are explicit, quick responses.
hypotheses.text: Technical failures and customer drop-offs are slow because they involve timeouts or abandoned sessions rather than quick explicit responses.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Technical failures averaged 17,422 ms of authorization latency across 23,887 failed attempts.
recommendations.rationale: Reducing slow technical failures would shorten checkout waits and could recover some payments.
recommendations.text: Investigate the technical failure category first, since it has both the highest average latency and a sizeable failure count.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The attempt data only begins on 2026-08-01, so the 'past two years' covers about three months (2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31).
recommendations.rationale: Only about three months of data exist, and a blended average would hide the large differences between failure types.
recommendations.text: Re-run this analysis once more history is available, and decide whether a single blended average or a per-category view is what you want to track.
